question: In 2019, ______ became the 24th Chief of the Naval Staff of India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Admiral Karambir Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Admiral Karambir Singh** became the 24th Chief of the Naval Staff of India on 31 May 2019.
 
• He succeeded **Admiral Sunil Lanba**, who served as the 23rd Chief of the Naval Staff.
 
• Admiral Karambir Singh is a helicopter pilot and has extensive experience in various command, staff, and instructional appointments.
 
• Before becoming the Chief of the Naval Staff, he served as the Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Eastern Naval Command.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS)**

 
 
• The Chief of the Naval Staff is the highest-ranking officer of the Indian Navy and the principal naval advisor to the President of India and the Government of India.
 
• The position is a four-star Admiral and the CNS is responsible for the command, control, and administration of the Indian Navy.
 
• The CNS is appointed by the President of India and typically serves a tenure of three years or until the age of 62, whichever is earlier.
 
• The CNS plays a crucial role in shaping the strategic direction, operational readiness, and modernization of the Navy.
 
 
 
• **Indian Navy**
 
 
• The Indian Navy is the naval branch of the Indian Armed Forces, tasked with safeguarding India's maritime borders and interests.
 
• It operates under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India.
 
• The Indian Navy is a blue-water navy, capable of operating in deep waters and projecting power across the seas.
 
• It plays a significant role in ensuring the security of India's maritime trade routes, conducting humanitarian missions, and participating in international maritime cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Naval Command**
 
 
• The Eastern Naval Command is one of the three major commands of the Indian Navy, headquartered in Visakhapatnam.
 
• It is responsible for the naval defense and operations in the eastern seaboard of India, including the Bay of Bengal and parts of the Indian Ocean.
 
• It plays a crucial role in maintaining maritime security, conducting naval exercises, and supporting national and international maritime operations.
 
• The command is headed by the Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief (FOC-in-C) of the Eastern Naval Command.
